text:
anya: Heads-up — I’m rolling out a small experiment called "delayed-free slab handoff" to address fragmentation and transient OOMs when KV-heavy requests spike. Goal: avoid eager return-to-free-list for certain slabs until a safe handoff point (batch drain / kv-commit).

sam: ok what's the heuristic for "safe handoff"?

anya: heuristic is based on two signals: 1) batcher.is_empty() and 2) kv_pending_commit == 0. If both true we perform slab handoff, otherwise we keep in a short-lived staging list for up to 50ms.

mike: curious about worst-case memory growth. keeping slabs for 50ms could increase peak a bit?

anya: measured +2% GPU working set on our 8-card canary, but tail OOMs dropped a lot. Tradeoff seems OK.

lee: did you try making the staging list per-stream instead of global? global seemed to cause head-of-line blocking in my earlier experiments.

anya: yes — staging list is per-device and then per-stream within device. We do lightweight striping so one noisy stream doesn't hold everything.

sam: also watch kernel selection interplay: if we delay frees we might keep workspace allocations alive and force different kernel code-path (e.g., multi-head fused kernels that need larger workspace). That can unexpectedly increase latency.

anya: good catch — so we added a compact_size threshold. If slab size > compact_size we trigger an eager compaction attempt (try_shrink_workspace) before staging. That avoids keeping huge workspaces pinned.

sophia: can you paste the config snippet? would like to add to oncall playbook for quick rollback.

anya: sure — snippet I used in canary:

```
# runtime.cfg
allocator.delayed_free.enabled = true
allocator.delayed_free.max_hold_ms = 50
allocator.delayed_free.compact_threshold_bytes = 8MB
allocator.delayed_free.per_stream_stripe = true
```

sam: nice. what's the canary scope and results?

anya: canary: 3 production pods serving large-context chat workload (kv cache hot), ran 24h. Results vs baseline: 
- transient OOM events: down 85%
- 99th latency for generate: down 6%
- mean GPU memory: +2%
- frequency of allocator fragmentation spikes (measured by free-run large_slab_count): down 70%

lee: those are convincing numbers. how about interactions with batching heuristics — did you see any increased batching delay because staging held buffers longer?

anya: minimal. batcher respects max_wait_ms, and we added a small hook so batcher proactively steals from staging list if it needs a buffer to keep latency SLOs. so staging is mostly a safety valve, not a blocker.

mike: did you profile with nsys to see if the extra refcount ops added noticeable CPU overhead?

anya: yes — traced a hotspot where handoff refcounting cost ~30us per handoff on CPU but we amortize by grouping handoffs at drain points. overall CPU spent on handoffs <0.5% of pod CPU.

sam: any changes in KV cache eviction patterns? holding slabs could mask eviction pressure and delay actual memory reclaimed for KV writes.

anya: we instrumented kv_eviction_lag; median unchanged, but tail improved because we avoided fragmentation-induced eviction churn. essentially fewer small fragments meant large contiguous allocations succeed.

sophia: rollback plan? if this regresses, how do we disable quickly?

anya: toggle allocator.delayed_free.enabled = false via runtime flags. deploy-bot also added a canary monitor that will auto-disable if OOM rate increases 2x in 10m.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for config: allocator.delayed_free.enabled=true on cluster-prod-3 at 2026-03-18T10:12:00Z. Monitoring OOMs, latency, memory. :robot_face:

mike: any follow-ups you want from infra team? I can allocate a jumbo pod to stress test worst-case sequences (many small allocs + interleaved kv writes).

anya: yes please — jumbo pod with 48GB streams and a synthetic workload that alternates long-context generation and kv writes (burst every 200ms). I'll send the harness.

lee: also run kernel-selection matrix: sequence lengths [64,512,2048] x batch sizes [1,4,8] to ensure we don't regress a kernel fallback. We've seen delayed frees force the runtime to pick fallback kernels before.

anya: noted — will include kernel matrix and nsys traces.

sam: great work. one more thought: consider exposing a consumer-level metric allocator.staging_count and allocator.staging_bytes so we can create alerts if staging grows beyond expected.

anya: good idea — added to canary dashboard already.

sophia: thanks. tagging @oncall for awareness.

anya: thanks all — will post results + traces in this thread when the 48h stress finishes. :white_check_mark:
